results.title: Dia Browser | Your setup, your way
results.content:
# Your setup, your way

Everyone's Dia looks a little different: what you keep pinned, what you bookmark, and how quickly you move. This week’s release focuses on making your space behave the way you want (and need it to). With improvements to layout, organization, and performance, Dia moves with you as your setup evolves.

Tab groups are auto-pinned

Creating a Tab Group is usually intentional: You have a project, a theme, or something you want to return to. Dia now reflects that by **automatically pinning new tab groups** when they’re created.

This keeps important groups anchored in your tabs (kinda like how Folders worked in Arc 👀) and reduces the need to constantly reorganize as your tab list grows.

Better window restoration

Accidentally closing a window shouldn’t mean losing your tabs, your hard work, or your customized set up.

You can now reopen a closed window from the File menu and get all of your tabs back in **one click**. No digging through your history or manually reopening tabs one by one required!

A cleaner, more intentional Bookmarks Bar

The Bookmarks Bar now only shows Tab Groups you’ve explicitly closed and moved there. Before, it showed all Tab Groups, even ones still open in other windows. Now, what you see reflects your intent—plus, it keeps your setup tidy and easier to manage.

Improved tab spacing and readability

When you’re organizing your space visually, even the little layout details matter. Groups now display more cleanly and predictably.

We fixed a tab truncation issue in the Tab Strip when Tab Groups are present to improve spacing and label clarity.

Dark incognito windows

When you’re switching contexts (or going undercover 🕵️), visual cues matter. Incognito windows now launch in **dark mode by default**. This makes it easier to recognize where you are, especially when you’re moving quickly between windows.

Performance Updates

Startup is now significantly faster on lower-spec machines!

We found that large favicon caches could grow to tens of thousands of entries over time, which slows down startup on machines with limited memory or slower storage. By capping the cache at 1,000 entries (more than enough for everyday use) launch is now nearly instantaneous after the first run.

That’s it for this week. What’s one small change that’s made your setup work better for you? Tweet us the answer and we’ll include it on a future release note!

results.title: Dia Browser | Conversations, Context, and Chat
results.content:
# Conversations, Context, and Chat

Work happens across tabs, apps, and conversations in the office. At Dia, we’re bringing everything you need—the who, the what, and the where—into your browser, so you spend less time gathering info and more time doing the work you care about. With this release, all that context is one mention away in **Chat**.

Slack Search

Skip the DMs and search Dia. Just attach the Slack tool to chat, type your question into the search, and watch results come in from your workspace. Get quick summaries and important intel immediately—now you don’t have to comb through Slack to figure out the latest with the feature (the one you heard about in that meeting) that’s kind of like what you’re working on.

Whether you’re using Slack in browser or app, the search works. And this won’t mess with your Slack state—messages won’t be marked as read and your history won’t be saved.

Slack Search Tool in Chat

A few more updates

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/e1b5b00aed9f162a0985fed24167ffcc7393d047-1500x900.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

from the desk of

Rosey, Engineering Manager

Alongside our new Slack integration, today’s release brings a few more under-the-hood upgrades to Chat — from better voice input to stronger memory and more. All designed to bring your work and your context, into one place. Seamlessly! Tell us what’s landing with you, and where you want us to go next

Improved voice transcription

Voice just got better in Dia. We’ve moved to streaming transcription for more accurate recordings and precise punctuation, especially when you’ve got a lot to say. Bring on the long recordings. 🗣️

See what Chat is doing with your tabs

Chat now shows each tabs-related tool call—what it read, opened, and closed—and gives you a deterministic way to act on those tabs and URLs. More power, with the receipts.

Automatic Memory Search is now truly automatic

Dia now searches memory more reliably, triggering on many more prompts that reference past events or out‑of‑context knowledge. No need for @mentions or exact phrasing—if at first it don't succeed, it'll try, try again.

results.title: Dia Browser | Live Tab Groups are here
results.content:
# Live Tab Groups are here

This is a step toward something new—the idea that your browser can automatically surface the work that matters right now, and let it fade away when it doesn’t.

Engineers, you know how it goes: you open a PR, wait for reviews, then merge. But then PR notifications get buried under email, calendar, chat, and other pings, and you have to go digging for them. That is, until this week, with the release of **Live Tab Groups**.

We're starting with GitHub, but this is the first **Live Tab Groups** launch of many. All designed to keep your most important work front and center in Dia.

Github Live Tab Groups

Now, the moment you open a pull request, Dia creates a **GitHub** **Live Group** in your sidebar. No set up required, simply create your PR.

The first time, you’ll see a quick introductory popover explaining what’s new. The **Live Tab Group** shows both the pull requests you’ve opened, and ones waiting on your review. It stays pinned by default, so your work is always visible even as you hop into meetings or switch projects.

As work moves forward (or merges), the Live Tab Group updates itself.

New pull requests appear when you open them, and closed or merged ones drop off, so you’re not maintaining a mental or manual checklist.

When pull requests close, they leave the Live Tab Group automatically.

No cleanup required.

If Dia is unable to fetch the latest status from Github, there will be a visual cue to reauthenticate. That way, instead of refreshing and wondering what’s wrong, you know exactly what to do to get things syncing again.

Prefer a more hands-on approach? A dedicated right-click menu lets you refresh the **Live Tab Group** and configure what repos or PRs show up.

All of this means less time tracking down links, digging through your PR page, or remembering which PRs are still on you. And of course, more time to actually review and ship changes.

Help us build what's next

results.title: Dia Browser | A closer look
results.content:
# A closer look

Open Dia this week and it might look the same. But take a closer peek, and you'll notice—things are tidier, quieter, more considered. This week’s updates don’t announce themselves, but once you start noticing them, your Dia experience is *that***** much better.

A more scannable sidebar

Spacing is tighter, labels are clearer, and the font size is a bit bigger and easier to read. It’s the same sidebar you know, just cleaner, calmer, and easier on the eyes.

A refreshed Tab Switcher

The Tab Switcher got an updated layout with new colors and shadows. The switcher now hides tabs you haven't visited in a while. So when you press **Ctrl+Tab**, you flip through what you're actually using, not every tab ever opened

A browser that blends in

Dia should feel less like a frame around your content and more like an extension of it. The top band of your browser now picks up the color of the site you're visiting, and keeps up as the page changes beneath it, even after you scroll.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/724a55bd552f613cf51096ab5338a8a5c5895f5f-950x709.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Preferences that travel with you

With Sync, your settings now follow you. Set your Tabs, Privacy, Profiles, Memory, Shortcuts, and more on one machine, and they're already waiting on the other. One Dia, every device.

Sometimes the best updates are the ones that make everything feel a touch better. Drop us a line on [Twitter](https://x.com/diabrowser) and tell us what you notice.
